subject: spanish

rounds.lie: “No me gusta nada” means “I quite like it”.
rounds.why: “No me gusta nada” means “I don’t like it at all”. “I quite like it” is “me gusta bastante”.
rounds.truth: “No me gusta nada” means “I don’t like it at all”.
truths: “Me chifla el cine” means “I love the cinema” (colloquial).
“Prefiero la música pop” means “I prefer pop music”.

rounds.lie: “Las películas de terror me dan miedo” means “horror films make me laugh”.
rounds.why: “Dar miedo” means “to frighten”, so it means horror films “scare me”; making you laugh is “dar risa”.
rounds.truth: “Las películas de terror me dan miedo” means “horror films scare me”.
truths: “Quedar con amigos” means “to meet up with friends”.

rounds.why: “Tocar” is only for instruments; sports use “jugar”: “juego al fútbol”.
truths: “Toco el piano” means “I play the piano”.
“Veo series en mi móvil” means “I watch series on my phone”.

rounds.lie: “Nos llevamos mal” means “We get on well”.
rounds.why: “Llevarse mal” = to get on badly. “We get on well” is “nos llevamos bien”.
rounds.truth: “Nos llevamos mal” means “We get on badly”.
truths: “Me apoya siempre” means “He/she always supports me”.

rounds.why: “Nochevieja” is New Year’s Eve. Christmas Eve is “Nochebuena”.
truths: “Los Reyes Magos” means “the Three Kings (Wise Men)”.
“Las Fallas” is a festival celebrated in Valencia.
“Me llevo bien con mis padres” means “I get on well with my parents”.
“Soy hijo único” means “I am an only child”.

rounds.lie: The ending “simpáticas” describes a group of boys.
rounds.why: The “-as” ending is feminine plural, so it describes girls/women. A group of boys would be “simpáticos”.
rounds.truth: The ending “simpáticas” describes a group of girls/women.
